audit_findings.title: Known 2026 margin headwind is absent from the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $55 million expected 2026 gross-profit headwind, equal to 23.2% of the $236.6 million OE anchor; net OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Reduces the forward owner-earnings starting level before scenario growth is applied, with the lower earnings then affecting every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Management expects these dynamics to negatively impact gross profit by $25 million to $35 million in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated: the valuation starts from unadjusted FY2025 OE even though the latest 10-Q raises the expected 2026 CID-related headwind from $25-$35 million to approximately $55 million. First-half 2026 gross profit declined only $2.8 million and net income increased $2.0 million, showing partial offsets, but the filing does not quantify sustainable mitigation. Because the disclosed gross-profit pressure is nearly one-quarter of anchor OE, the unresolved net reduction is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 OE to first-half 2026 results and full-year guidance, quantify sustainable SG&A and higher-margin-therapy offsets, reset OE by the resulting after-tax net headwind, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Growth-related working-capital investment may be omitted
audit_findings.magnitude: $116.539 million 2025 net cash investment in receivables and inventory after accounts-payable funding, equal to 49.3% of anchor OE; first-half 2026 produced a $36.213 million net release on the same items
audit_findings.mechanism: Required incremental operating working capital should reduce owner earnings or forecast cash flow as revenue grows.
audit_findings.evidence: The change was also largely related to an increase in accounts receivable driven by revenue growth.
audit_findings.explanation: The model omission is demonstrated because the $236.6 million anchor closely follows net income plus depreciation and amortization less property capex and does not show a working-capital charge. The enduring amount remains unresolved: 2025 used $54.593 million for receivables and $81.469 million for inventory, partly funded by a $19.523 million accounts-payable increase, while first-half 2026 reversed $36.213 million through these items. Even after acknowledging strategic inventory timing, the 2025 scale is large enough that a normalized recurring requirement could change value materially, especially in the 3% and 6% growth cases.
audit_findings.action: Separate strategic inventory timing from recurring balances, calculate normalized net operating working capital as a percentage of incremental revenue, deduct scenario-specific investment, and rerun the DCF.

audit_findings.title: Temporary interest-rate hedge benefit may be capitalized indefinitely
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.638 million pretax and approximately $6.34 million after tax in 2025; computed DCF effect of approximately $0.49-$0.68 per share if the entire benefit is removed
audit_findings.mechanism: Expiration of the cap can increase retained equity-level interest expense and reduce owner earnings after November 2026.
audit_findings.evidence: In October 2021, the Company entered into an interest rate cap hedge with a notional amount of $ 300.0 million for a five-year term beginning November 30, 2021.
audit_findings.explanation: The temporary benefit embedded in FY2025 is demonstrated, but its scale is not sufficient by itself to change the scenario conclusions. Applying the filed 26.6% tax rate and each scenario's existing PV-to-anchor multiple gives an estimated reduction of roughly $0.49 per share in bear, $0.58 in base and $0.68 in bull. Those amounts do not reverse the base case being below the $24.21 market price, the bull case being above it, or the buy-below conclusion. Moreover, first-half 2026 net interest expense improved as the term-loan rate fell, partly offsetting the declining hedge benefit.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the cap strike and exact expiration economics, apply a scenario-consistent post-expiry SOFR rate to the $672.915 million variable-rate balance, and rerun the interest normalization to verify that the effect remains within this scale.

audit_findings.title: Unbilled receivables create an earnings-quality risk
audit_findings.magnitude: $155.1 million gross unbilled receivables at December 2025, up $49.8 million or 47.3%; potential adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Unsupported revenue or price-concession estimates would reduce reported earnings and OE, while delayed collection increases working-capital investment.
audit_findings.evidence: Included in accounts receivable are earned but unbilled gross receivables of $ 155.1 million and $ 105.3 million as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: No revenue error is demonstrated. The gross unbilled balance rose much faster than 2025 revenue and represented 32.7% of year-end net receivables, so a meaningful failure of billing, collection or transaction-price estimates could affect value. However, unbilled receivables were essentially unchanged at $154.9 million in June 2026, and the filings provide no subsequent-collection or reversal data. The record therefore cannot establish either the amount or materiality of any misstatement.
audit_findings.action: Obtain an aging and subsequent-billing roll-forward for the December 2025 balance, cash collections through the latest available date, write-offs and concession true-ups, then reduce OE and working-capital assumptions for any demonstrated shortfall.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-dependent growth could require unmodeled cash reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $117.247 million 2025 acquisition cash outlay, equal to 49.6% of anchor OE; future acquisition requirement unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition cash needed to produce forecast growth would be a reinvestment outflow not captured by ordinary property capex, reducing equity cash flow and value.
audit_findings.evidence: We continue to evaluate acquisition opportunities and view acquisitions as a key part of our growth strategy.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking dependency rather than a demonstrated valuation error. Management calls acquisitions a key growth strategy, and the FY2025 anchor includes almost a full year of Intramed Plus earnings after a $117.247 million cash acquisition. Nevertheless, management described 2025 revenue growth as primarily organic, and no acquisition spending occurred in first-half 2026. The record does not establish that either the 3% or 6% forecast requires acquisitions, but the historical transaction shows that the omitted cash requirement could be substantial if acquisition-led growth is assumed later.
audit_findings.action: Require an explicit organic-versus-acquired growth bridge for each scenario; if acquisitions contribute, estimate recurring purchase consideration and integration costs and deduct them before rerunning the affected scenarios.
